## 1. Fixed object, exact quantifiers and the consumer gap

Use the same fixed raw chart X=c+Z^6 of the restricted Cell occupancy model. A state is a finite-support function X -> N0. A site retains all six coordinates; time is separately typed and unused. For i=1,...,6, M_i sums over a coordinate-i fiber and retains the other five coordinates JOINTLY. Put v=(1,1,1,1,1,1); N_v sums over cosets of Z v. Write O=(M_1,...,M_6,N_v). All original bins, including zero bins, are retained. No boundary coarsening or changed observer is permitted.

For a finite integer signed array h, define h_+=max(h,0), h_-=max(-h,0) coefficientwise. If Oh=0, summing any M_i gives total(h)=0, so its move mass is

    mu(h)=sum h_+=sum h_-=(1/2)sum |h|.

Define the COMPLETE library

    C={nonzero finite integer h on X : Oh=0 and mu(h)<=63}.

It includes every eligible move, not a selected finite palette. Its defining conditions are invariant under integer translation and sign. There is NO range, diameter or box restriction on a library member. An edge adds one member of C when the destination is nonnegative. Both signs are already included. Every path uses finite nonnegative configurations and preserves the same seven readouts and total mass at each individual edge. No temporary negatives, simultaneous illegal batch or excursion outside the observer fiber is allowed. The graph of all configurations may have infinitely many vertices.

The precise conclusion is:

1. Every observer fiber of common mass below63 is a singleton. Any two distinct states in a fiber of common mass63 are joined by one C edge.
2. At common mass64 there is an explicit pair of distinct states in one fiber, both isolated for this ENTIRE library C. Thus64 is the first mass where this library fails to connect all fibers.

This asks about a cap on MOVE MASS, while allowing unbounded move ranges. It differs from the author's earlier fixed-configuration-mass / uniformly bounded-range / selected-background argument. That earlier argument is not a premise here. It also differs from the old critical-mass palette iff, which concerns configuration mass63 only.

The closest new accepted input proves connection and its obstruction on one specified finite box, using actual moves supported on that box. It explicitly leaves infinite-chart higher-mass connection outside its scope. The logical bridge still owed here is that nonnegativity and the full original readouts prevent a path from escaping that box. Signed-lattice spanning or the old boxed verdict alone does not pay that obligation.

## 3. Full readouts and nonnegativity force confinement

Lemma. Let B0=product_(k=1)^6 [l_k,u_k] be a finite box in the fixed INTEGER index chart. Suppose a finite N0 state f is supported on c+B0 and q is another finite N0 state with Oq=Of. Then q is also supported on c+B0.

Proof. Suppose q(c+y)>0 for some y outside B0. Choose a coordinate k with y_k outside [l_k,u_k], and choose i different from k. The coordinate-deletion map pi_i retains coordinate k. Every occupied point of f has its retained k coordinate in the stated interval, so

    (M_i f)(pi_i y)=0.

The corresponding nonnegative sum for q contains its strictly positive contribution q(c+y). Hence (M_i q)(pi_i y)>=q(c+y)>0, contradicting equality of the complete M_i readouts. This excludes every outside occupied point and proves the lemma.

Only the old full coordinate-fiber readouts and nonnegativity are used here. The original seventh readout stays present but is not needed to prevent escape. The argument is not valid for signed intermediate states or for readouts that omit/coarsen the zero bins. It supplies an actual support restriction on every vertex in the same fiber, not just on an initial comparison or on a proposed palette.

## 4. The unrestricted-range library fails at mass64

Take the accepted box B from Section2 and its actual coefficient arrays g0,g1,g01. Let

    F=(g01)_-, H=(g01)_+.

The boxed input proves F and H are distinct N0 states, each of mass64, with OF=OH and support inside c+B. Each has total occupancy16 at each x-level0,1,2,3.

Suppose an edge from F using some k in C were legal. Its destination q=F+k is finite and nonnegative, and Oq=OF because Ok=0. The confinement lemma forces q to stay inside c+B. Since F also stays there, the signed difference k=q-F is supported inside c+B as well. This is the crucial bridge: a globally allowed move cannot evade the boxed classification by creating an outside intermediate state.

Now k is a nonzero integer boxed comparison of mass at most63. Statement(A) therefore gives k in {g0,-g0,g1,-g1}. Any of the first two choices consumes31 negative units from x-level1; any of the last two consumes31 from x-level2. F has only16 TOTAL units at each such level. Legality would require F>=k_- site by site and hence at least31 units at the required level, a contradiction. Thus no C edge starts at F. Exactly the same proof applies to H, whose four layer totals are the same. The library is sign-closed, so an incoming edge could be reversed; there is no incident edge in either direction.

Consequently F and H are isolated vertices of the same observer fiber even for the COMPLETE infinite library C, with every translation and every range allowed. No finite legal path connects them. This conclusion uses the full boxed kernel/mass classification only AFTER the confinement bridge. It does not infer global nonconnection by silently imposing a box restriction on the allowed moves.

## 5. All smaller masses, and why64 is the first failure

Let f,g have the same seven readouts and common mass M<=63. If they are distinct, h=g-f is a nonzero finite integer kernel array. At every negative site h_-=max(f-g,0)<=f; hence mu(h)<=M.

If M<63, this contradicts the accepted unbounded sharp lower bound mu(h)>=63. Thus each such fiber is a singleton and is connected by a zero-length path.

If M=63, h has mu(h)<=63 and belongs to C by definition. The single step f+h=g is legal because the specified destination is nonnegative. Thus any two distinct states in that fiber are connected directly. This uses neither the full mass63 equality classification nor a finite selected palette. Zero or coincident states are already covered by the zero-length path.

Combining this with Section4 proves the precise first-failure claim. It does NOT prove that moves of mass at most64 suffice at every higher configuration mass, or determine the optimal move degree of a universal connecting library on the whole chart.
